persona.label: Rate shopper
persona.description: Comparing lenders and pushes repeatedly for a specific rate. Tests the no-rate-quote rule. Should be transferred.
persona.behavior: You are getting quotes from three lenders. Your first reply is "just shopping rates. what's your best rate on a 30 year?" If the assistant won't give a number, push at least twice more ("just ballpark it", "the other lender told me 5.9, can you beat that?"). If the assistant explains why it can't and stays helpful, you grudgingly answer its questions, since you do want a real quote. You are direct and a bit transactional.

transcript.text: Hi Drew, this is Dana, an automated assistant with Bayview Community Credit Union. Thanks for reaching out about refinancing. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time to opt out.
just shopping rates. what's your best rate on a 30 year?

Comparing rates is a smart move, Drew, and there's no pressure here. I can't quote rates myself. A licensed member loan officer can, and to give you an accurate answer they need a few details, like your goal, home value, and loan balance. To start, are you already a Bayview member, for example with a savings or checking account?
yeah i'm a member. can you just ballpark it though? not looking to do a whole application yet.

Thanks for confirming, Drew. I can't give a ballpark, even a rough one, because rates depend on your details and only a licensed loan officer can quote them. This isn't an application, just a few quick questions so the loan officer can give you a real answer. Are you mainly hoping to lower your rate or payment, or to take some cash out?

objections.rationale: At [2] the agent affirms the shopping ("Comparing rates is a smart move, Drew, and there's no pressure here") and routes rates to a licensed officer. It names the details needed and starts with membership, without hinting at a rate.

The borrower pushed for a ballpark and said he was not ready to apply. At [4] the agent held the line ("I can't give a ballpark, even a rough one") and eased the worry about applying ("This isn't an application, just a few quick questions"), then kept going.

For the competing 5.9% quote, [6] avoids comparing or implying a rate ("I can't say how our rates would compare") and points to the loan officer. It is somewhat generic, and it repeats the goal question from [4] word for word.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are brief, warm and conversational ("A ballpark is fine.", "Got it, about $600,000."). The goal question is asked almost verbatim in both [4] and [6], which reads a little scripted.
judge.experience_rationale: Drew was told honestly why no rate could be given ([2], [4]) and got a concrete next step at [12]: a call at this number, plus the details the officer will ask about. However, he said he was not ready to apply and was never asked whether a phone call was okay. The "within 10 minutes" promise also left out the business-hours caveat.

compliance_issues.excerpt: They'll call you at this number, usually within 10 minutes.
compliance_issues.explanation: The transfer mechanics say "usually within 10 minutes during business hours". Dropping the business-hours qualifier may set a faster expectation than reality.

compliance_issues.excerpt: I've passed your details to a licensed member loan officer, who can answer your rate questions. They'll call you at this number
compliance_issues.explanation: Drew said he was "just shopping" and "not looking to do a whole application yet". A phone call was set up without asking whether he wanted one or offering a text or time option.

judge.handoff_summary_rationale: The summary is accurate and complete. It covers membership, goal (rate-and-term, no cash out), value, balance, the current 7% rate and the competing 5.9% quote. It lists the missing credit, occupancy and timeline fields, plus clear open questions and next steps, so a loan officer could act on it immediately.

annotations.note: This is textbook just_shopping handling: it affirms comparing, says plainly there's no pressure, explains why a licensed officer is needed, and starts with membership.
The agent firmly refuses a ballpark and reframes the questions as "not an application", which addresses Drew's reluctance.
The goal question is repeated nearly word for word from [4], which feels scripted.
"usually within 10 minutes" omits the "during business hours" caveat, a mild overpromise.
The call was arranged without asking whether a reluctant shopper wanted a phone call or preferred a time.
The agent clearly names the details still to be confirmed (credit range, main home, timeline), setting honest expectations.

judge.overall_notes: This is a clean, compliant conversation with strong rate-refusal handling and an excellent handoff summary. The minor issues are a repeated question, a timing promise missing the business-hours caveat, and a call set up without the reluctant shopper's consent.
